 UST ousts Ateneo in men's play, stays perfect in women's side
 Nov 16, 2026
 6:59 AM GMT+8
 The UAAP Facebook photo
 MANILA – University of Santo Tomas eliminated Ateneo de Manila University after an 89-84 win in the UAAP Season 89 men’s basketball at Smart Araneta Coliseum in Quezon City on Sunday.
 The Growling Tigers improved to 7-6 with their third straight win, moving half a game of third-running Far Eastern University Tamaraws and De La Salle University Archers, both at 7-5.
 National University and University of the Philippines, both at 9-3, have advanced but the twice-to-beat bonus for the top two teams is still up for grabs.
 The defending champion Archers eliminated the Adamson University Falcons, 84-69, in the other game.
 “Every single game is a do-or-die for us and it shows in the way we play,” UST assistant coach Peter Martin said.
 Collins Akowe scored 16 points on 6-of-7 shooting and hauled down nine rebounds in 34 minutes for UST.
 The Growling Tigers saw their 13-point lead reduced to two, 76-74, with 5 minutes and 34 seconds remaining.
 Ateneo stayed within striking distance at 81-78 with 2:38 left, until Mark Llemit scored on a goaltending call against Sultan Baruwa and Amiel Acido nailed a triple with 34.2 seconds left to seal the win.
 Ateneo, with its fourth straight loss, and Adamson are out of the semifinal race at 5-8.
 Top Ateneo rookie Kieffer Alas missed the game due to an allergic attack, while his father, coach Louie Alas, served the second of his two-game suspension.
 UST faces Adamson while Ateneo closes out its campaign against also-ran University of the East (1-12) on Nov. 25.
 In the women's division, defending champion UST also got Ateneo's number to prevail, 87-80, and extend its perfect run to 12 games
 The Tigresses will take on Season 88 runners-up National University Lady Bulldogs on Nov. 22, the first of their final two games.
 An outright finals berth awaits if the Tigresses sweep the eliminations.
 The Blue Eagles ended their three-game winning streak and fell to 6-6 and into a tie for fourth place with the FEU Lady Tamaraws. (PNA)
